Live: Captain, first officer of flydubai flight hospitalised, says Saudi's Tabuk Airportflydubai Flight Incident Live Updates: A commercial Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv, Israel, made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after transmitting emergency alerts shortly after takeoff. According to publicly available flight-tracking data, the aircraft first issued a 7700 squawk code, signalling a general emergency, before transmitting a 7500 code associated with a hijacking or unlawful interference. Israeli officials suspect the incident may have involved an attempt to take control of the aircraft and crash it in an act of terrorism. People who were aboard the plane and their relatives told Hebrew-language media that the co-pilot stabbed the captain in the cockpit, causing the aircraft to plunge about 17,000 feet in less than a minute. A group of Israeli passengers reportedly entered the cockpit, subdued the attacker and helped stabilise the aircraft. The plane, carrying about 180 passengers, most of them Israeli, later landed safely in Saudi Arabia. Follow this live blog for the latest updates on the Flydubai flight incident.
